newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Albright leaves SE Asia after blast at Mahathir.
newsitem.headline: Albright leaves SE Asia after blast at Mahathir.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright headed home from Singapore on Wednesday after a visit to Southeast Asia during which she brushed off criticisms of the West by Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
"I think that Dr Mahathir is a case of his own," she said after major regional meetings in Malaysia which Mahathir opened with an attack on "unscrupulous" Western currency speculators.

Albright said she felt she had struck a resonant chord among ASEAN foreign ministers at the Malaysia meetings, adding that not all members of Mahathir's generation of leaders in their seventies shared his perspective.

"I think, frankly, that I articulated what some of them had been thinking and were more willing to admit than I had expected that the process in Burma had been slower than they would have liked," she told reporters on Tuesday .
The U.S. has urged faster progress on democracy and human rights in Burma, which was formally admitted into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) along with Laos on July 23.

Albright was in Singapore for less than 24 hours after the ASEAN conferences. She met with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar and former Singapore prime minister Lee Kuan Yew.
She cited talks on Tuesday with Lee -- himself a frequent critic of the West in general and the U.S. in particular -- as a highlight of her Asian tour.
Albright and Singapore officials said the visit had strengthened bilateral ties, although she did raise human rights issues with Goh.
Investment and trade ties between the United States and Singapore are extensive, and Singapore provides logistics support and repair facilities for U.S. naval forces in the region.
ASEAN also groups Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam.
